findings.issue: Cell 15 (figure `plots_v2/spectra_analysis/online_energy_discarded.pdf/.png`) plots x = `np.linspace(0, 1, len(step))[idx]` and labels it "Training progress". `step` is the LOGGED-step array, and I read the schedule straight from the npz: `svs_step` = every step for 0..1000 then every 20th (toy: 1262 logged of 6240 steps; unique diffs {1: 1000, 20: 261}). So index-fraction 0.5 = step 630 = 10% of toy training, 0.75 = step 945 = 15%, and the whole last 80% of training is compressed into x in [0.8, 1.0]. The dramatic toy jump the figure shows at x ~ 0.80-0.85 sits exactly at the dense/sparse boundary (index 1010/1262 = 0.80, step ~1000 = 16% of training), and the CIFAR curves' onset at x ~ 0.6-0.75 is step ~800-1000 = 11-14% of training, so the figure's visual claim ("the cut starts discarding late in training") is wrong as read. The distortion also differs per scan (dense 1000 of 1262 logged points on toy/poly, 1000 of 1731 on MNIST, 1000 of 1220 on nanoGPT), so the seven curves are not aligned on this axis either; and `sv.smooth(..., 25)` is a 25-SAMPLE window = 25 steps in the dense region but 500 steps in the sparse region, so the apparent sharpness changes along each curve. The frozen helper does it correctly for per-step curves (`sv_diagnostics._x_axis` over the full-length `num_nonzero_svs`), so this cell is also inconsistent with comparisons.ipynb's `x_progress=True` panels.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the real step axis: `x = a['step'] / d.n_steps` (or plot against `step` on a log axis), and smooth in step units rather than in samples. While in this cell, fix the layout too: with `loc='center left', bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, .5)` plus `tight_layout()` the axes shrink to ~45% of the canvas and the default-size y-label overlaps the second title line in the rendered PNG - set the label/title font sizes or use `fig.subplots_adjust`.

findings.issue: Cells 5-6 pick each scan's learning rate with `scan.best_sven(k=scan.B)['lr']` and caption the result "best Sven lr per scan". For cifar10_resnet_ce_scan that returns lr=0.5 / rtol=0.3, which is a 3-of-5-seed run of the in-flight rtol extension, while the selection of record (bench/best_configs.json, generated 2026-09-20T03:58, full binding rule) is lr=0.1 / rtol=0.01. I confirmed both: `best_sven(k=128)` -> lr 0.5, rtol 0.3; and from the raw jsonl the live configs now lead on seed-mean final val (k128/lr0.5/rtol0.3 = 1.3537 with n_ok=3/3, k128/lr0.1/rtol0.1 = 1.3563 with 3/3, vs the selected k128/lr0.1/rtol0.01 = 1.4028 with 5/5). Consequences: (a) the CIFAR-CE row of RANK_TABLE and its curve in `rank_vs_rtol_and_batch` are at an lr the campaign does not select, and the values differ hugely from the selected lr - notebook prints used/B 0.6080 -> 0.2291 (rtol 1e-4 -> 0.3) whereas at the selected lr=0.1 I recompute 0.9717 -> 0.5577; (b) the implementer's report quotes "CIFAR-CE 0.97->0.56", i.e. the lr=0.1 numbers, which are NOT what its own notebook prints - a wrong number in the deliverable; (c) comparisons.ipynb prints no `headline.freshness_report()` banner at all even though it is the notebook whose numbers move (its own load says 767 records, my later load says 770, and 15-18 manifest entries are missing).
findings.suggested_fix: Drive the lr from the selection of record (`headline.selection_methods(scan)['SVD']`) or, if a live best is wanted, print both and say which is which; add `headline.freshness_report()` + the PROVISIONAL banner to comparisons.ipynb as spectra_analysis.ipynb does; and correct the 0.97->0.56 line in the report (or re-derive it at the lr the notebook actually uses).

findings.issue: `plot_probe_spectra` silently plots ONE seed: with `seed=None` it loads every cached trajectory and then uses `ents[0]` (mseed1000/2000/3000, first by sorted path). The notebook (cell 30) calls it with `seed=None` for all four probe scans, and neither the four `probe_spectra_<scan>` figures nor the section-9.1 markdown says a single seed is shown - while the online section 3 is explicit about exactly that point ("one seed - seeds are not averaged here"). A reader will take the probe-set spectrum evolution for a 5-seed result.
findings.suggested_fix: Either annotate the seed in the panel/figure title (`e['model_seed']`) or average the spectra over seeds (they are the same fixed matrix definition for every seed only after conditioning on the seed's init, so annotating is the honest option); raise or warn when more than one entry is returned and no seed was requested.

findings.issue: The (k, rtol) heatmap (cell 20, `online_used_rank_grid`) shows no seed count and no diverged count per cell, and `spectra_figs.used_rank_grid` drops runs with `diverged/failed` without counting them (it returns `n_seeds` but no attempted). Recomputed: at toy lr=0.01, 6 of 30 cells rest on fewer than 5 seeds - k=32/rtol=1e-6 is ONE seed (0.59 in the figure; 4 of 5 dropped), k=16/rtol=1e-6 one seed, k=8/rtol=1e-6 one seed, and the three 1e-5 cells four seeds - exactly the bottom-of-the-rtol-grid region where 194 of toy's Sven runs diverged (EXPERIMENTS.md section 7). CIFAR-CE has 3 of 9 cells at 3 seeds, and its blank k=64 cells at rtol>=0.03 (no runs at all) are unexplained in the caption. The binding convention says every table shows finished/attempted, and this is precisely the figure where robustness has to be shown honestly.
findings.suggested_fix: Annotate each cell with `n_seeds` (e.g. `0.59` over `n=1`) or hatch/grey cells with n_seeds<5, add a finished/attempted column to `used_rank_grid` (count the dropped diverged runs instead of skipping them), and say in the caption why the CIFAR-CE k=64 cells are empty.

findings.issue: The Codex-Low-4 verdict (cell 35) counts a statistical tie as a win. It prints "Sven is smallest on 2 of 4 scans" for `dist_init`, and one of those two is MNIST label-reg where Sven = 12.4761 and HIG = 12.5184. I recomputed from the raw npz: per-seed Sven-minus-HIG = [-0.107, -0.232, +0.177, +0.052, -0.101], mean -0.042 +/- 0.159 (ddof=1) - 2 of 5 seeds go the other way, and the seed stds are 0.269 (Sven) / 0.339 (HIG), i.e. six times the gap. The LOW4 table computes `std` in its `agg` but prints only means, ranks and `Sven / smallest`, so nothing on the page shows that this rank is noise (the only other "win", polynomial 7.52 vs 8.12, is a real 8%).
findings.suggested_fix: Print the seed std (or the paired per-seed difference vs the next-best method) beside each rank and treat overlaps as ties in the verdict line - e.g. "smallest on 1 of 4, tied with HIG on MNIST label-reg (-0.04 +/- 0.16 paired)".

findings.issue: Intro table (cell 0) states the probe-set spectra are "$\min(n_\text{rows}, P)$ (593-27,562)" wide. Actual widths from the cache: svals shape (34, 593) toy, (34, 673) polynomial, (35, 512) mnist_scan_ce, (35, 512) mnist_scan_labelRegression probe512 - i.e. 512-673, never 27,562 (that is MNIST's parameter count P, and the min is the 512 probe rows). As written it promises a spectrum that resolves ~27k directions on MNIST. Related smaller inconsistency in cell 27: it prints "mnist_scan_labelRegression: 24 cached trajectories" using `load_spectra` defaults, while everything downstream uses the 20 `probe512` ones (the 4 `probe2000_epochs` files are filtered out by `epochs_only=False`), so the printed inventory does not match the analysis.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the measured widths (512-673) in the intro table, and in cell 27 print `len(...)` under the same filters `probe_metrics` uses (or print the per-probe-tag breakdown).

findings.issue: Two probe metrics are plotted below the float64 resolution with no floor marked, unlike the online panels which draw the recorded Gram floor. (1) `cond` on toy is pinned to the arbitrary `PROBE_FLOOR = 1e-12`: I measured rank(sigma > 1e-12 sigma_max) = 13 -> 44 of 593 and cond 2.44e11 -> 6.38e11, i.e. the curve stays within a factor ~4 of the 1e12 cutoff while the raw sigma_min/sigma_max is 1.3e-17, so the toy panel of `probe_cond` mostly measures the threshold, not the Jacobian. (2) `sigma_B_over_1` on toy starts at sigma_32/sigma_1 = 9.5e-17 (single-seed check; the resolved rank at step 0 is 13, so sigma_32 does not numerically exist) and the section-9.2 markdown describes the whole curve as "the damping at Sven's batch cut".
findings.suggested_fix: Draw a `PROBE_FLOOR` line (and/or mask points where the index exceeds the resolved rank) on the `cond` and `sigma_B_over_1` panels, and say in the markdown that toy's spectrum is rank-deficient so both quantities are floor-limited there.

findings.issue: Three verifiable over-claims in the implementer's final report (not in the notebooks): "tests/test_spectra_figs.py (456 l, 31 tests)" - pytest collects and passes 23; "verify_rel_error <= 2e-8" for the 20 new mnist_scan_ce_diag npz - the max over the 20 files is 1.14e-7 (max abs 1.19e-8); "7e-2 MNIST-CE" discarded batch residual - that is the smoothed curve endpoint (I reproduce 7.26e-2 with the 25-sample window) while the table printed beside it gives 1 - 0.951657 = 4.8e-2 at the last logged step. findings.issue: The NORMS table (cell 23) uses `.round(5)`, so toy's `resid_norm` final and ratio both print as 0.00000 although the raw values are 3.47e-6 and 3.66e-7 (per-seed final resid_norm 1.46e-6 ... 9.78e-6) - a real and interesting five-decade collapse displayed as an exact zero, next to prose that reasons about "ratio < 1".
findings.suggested_fix: Format the table with `{:.3g}` / `to_string(float_format=...)` instead of `round(5)`.

findings.issue: `mechanism_table`'s `binds` label hard-codes "neither ($k=B$)" in the else-branch, which is reached whenever `used_final >= k - 0.5` and `k >= mean rtol_rank` - true today only for the k=B scans, but it would mislabel a k<B configuration whose rtol-rank happens to sit just under k (e.g. k=32, B=64, rtol-rank 31.8). The same conflation appears in section 6's markdown, "`used/k = 1` means $k$ is the binding cut; below 1 means `rtol` is": on the k=B rows of the heatmap (the top row of every panel) `used/k = 1` means NOTHING binds, which is what the table's own "neither ($k=B$)" column says. Related framing point: on the selected configs `k` binds on none of the seven scans (k=B was selected on 5 of 7), so the report's headline "on 5 of 7 scans rtol, not k, is the binding cut" is clearer stated as "the selection chose k=B on 5 of 7, and where k<B the rtol cut still binds".
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the label from the data (`'neither'` plus `' ($k=B$)'` only when `d.k == d.B`), and reword the section-6 sentence to distinguish `used/k = 1 and k < B` (k binds) from `used/k = 1 and k = B` (nothing binds).
